source.title: Stochastic collapse: how gradient noise attracts SGD dynamics towards simpler subnetworks
source.authors: Feng Chen; D. Kunin; Atsushi Yamamura; S. Ganguli

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares batch sizes and reports their effect on test loss in a linear teacher-student experiment, using a different setting from the large-batch studies named in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports effects of learning rate and label noise on network collapse and generalization. These do not test another listed version. The batch-size result is described in text but its values are shown only in Figure 11.
record.test_reason: The batch-size experiment measures synthetic linear regression at matched update steps, whereas V5 concerns image classifiers and language models under fixed epoch budgets. The image-model batch-size sweeps measure neuron collapse without reporting held-out performance. No own result tests another listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that SGD noise attracts networks toward simpler invariant subnetworks, demonstrate generalization benefits in a linear teacher-student framework, and connect prolonged early high-learning-rate training to improved subsequent generalization. Figure 11 reports better generalization with smaller batches in the synthetic setting.
record.recipe_differences: The batch-size comparison uses a linear teacher-student setup with synthetic noisy teacher signals and reports test loss; the version describes image classifiers and language models under fixed epoch budgets.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes test loss in the teacher-student experiment. The paper also reports complex shifts in neuron collapse across batch sizes in deep networks, but does not report generalization outcomes for those network batch-size sweeps.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller batches yield lower test loss in the synthetic linear teacher-student experiment, with a learning-rate drop at update step 53000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Smaller-batch SGD can improve generalization in noisy linear teacher-student regression under the tested update-based schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Longer initial training at a high learning rate improves subsequent image-classification test accuracy and accompanies fewer independent neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extending the initial high-learning-rate phase can improve later generalization through an accompanying simplification of the learned network.

fits_no_version.finding: Image-model batch-size sweeps produce complex changes in the fraction of independent neurons without reporting corresponding test performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size affects stochastic collapse in a model- and layer-dependent manner.

record.problems: The batch-size generalization result is described qualitatively and shown in a figure without numerical values in the text. Its setting is a linear teacher-student model with structured assumptions, so it does not directly establish the stated image-classification or language-model conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No other result directly tests a listed version. Figure 6 reports learning-rate schedule effects on deep-network test accuracy, but the listed versions do not test that intervention as such.

rows.subject: two-layer student network
rows.size_stated: input and output dimensions 64; hidden-layer dimension d = min{m, n}
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD using different batch sizes, without label noise, and evaluated before and after a learning-rate drop.

conditions.value: 53000 learning-rate drop; setup otherwise as Fig. 5

rows.value: Training with smaller batch sizes generalizes better; numerical values are figure only.
rows.note: The text states the direction of the effect; it does not give numerical test-loss values or specify the compared batch sizes here.
rows.check: Figure 11 explicitly reports better generalization with smaller batches, but this cannot establish V5: the subject is a linear regression student and the schedule uses update steps, not fixed epochs. The baseline should identify the larger-batch conditions; numerical losses and batch sizes are unavailable in the supplied text. Cite Appendix J for setup and Appendix K, Figure 11 for results. 'Without label noise' means no added training-time label noise; the fixed teacher-generated targets remain noise-corrupted.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
